title: A document's subtitle printed larger than its title
description:
The @media print block scales .doc-title to 18pt and .doc-meta to 10pt but never mentioned .doc-subtitle, which kept its screen value of 1.8rem. rem is measured against the root font size, not against the title beside it, so the subtitle printed at 21.6pt against the title's 18pt -- the student's name 20% larger than the assignment it belonged to.

Measured off a real hs2.pdf from cs234: title 24.0, subtitle 28.8.

Only the PDF was wrong, which is why it lasted. On screen the two were 2.2rem and 1.8rem, so the title was larger -- but only by 18%, and both were font-weight 700, which is not a hierarchy. The subtitle line is usually the longer of the two, so it took more space than the title and drew the eye.

The decks had this right from the first commit that introduced both: .deck-title 2.9rem/700 over .deck-subtitle 1.5rem with no weight of its own, a ratio of 0.52. The document rule has never changed since it was written.

Reported by the maintainer against hs2-Web-Intro.
acceptance_criteria: In the PDF the title draws at a larger font size than the subtitle, asserted against a real rendered PDF. On screen the subtitle is clearly subordinate rather than merely smaller, and does not match the title for weight. The subtitle stays larger than the byline.
close_reason:
Root cause was the print block naming some selectors and not their neighbours, so a pt size sat beside a rem one. Fixed in three places: .doc-subtitle gets a print size (13pt), h4/h5/h6 get print sizes (11/10.5/10pt) where the scale used to invert at h4, and h1-h6 get explicit screen sizes instead of inheriting Bootstrap's viewport-relative scale, which had h1 at 39.4px above the title's 35.2px. The subtitle also drops to 1.4rem/400 from 1.8rem/700 so it reads as subordinate rather than as a second title.

Verified on the reporter's own file: hs2.pdf title 24.0 / subtitle 17.3, was 24.0 / 28.8. Ten tests in tests/test_title_block.py, two of them measuring a real PDF; mutation-verified by removing each rule in turn. 186 tests pass, integration included.

Turned up stn-tum while auditing the decks for the same defect.

title: A package_sources-only doc package generates orphaned files and a pkg target that cannot run
description:
generate_package keys the shared page files off has_pages, which includes
package_sources, while get_generated_files and the doc-template injection both
key off docs/slides only. A doc package configured with package_sources and no
docs or slides falls in the gap twice.

1. Invisible generated files.
   generate.py:264 injects hidden-filter.lua, mermaid-figure-filter.lua,
   embed-images.lua, html-to-pdf.js and Dockerfile.browser whenever has_pages is
   true (generate.py:181 = docs or slides or package_sources).
   get_generated_files (generate.py:393) adds them only when
   `package.get("docs") or package.get("slides")`.

   Consequence: those five files are generated but invisible to `clean` and to
   the managed .gitignore section. They show up as untracked files in a course
   repo forever, and nothing removes them.

2. A pkg target that cannot run.
   html-template.html is injected only under `if context.get("has_docs")`
   (generate.py:275). But Makefile-pkg.j2:69 builds PKG_HTML with
   `$(DC) run --rm doc ...`, and pipeline.py:61 makes the doc service pass
   `--template=html-template.html`.

   Consequence: a package_sources-only doc package generates a `pkg` target
   whose pandoc invocation names a template that was never written. The target
   exists and fails.

Both edges are the same mistake: a predicate that says "this package renders
markdown" in one place and "this package has docs or slides" in the other. The
fix in both places is the same -- key the shared files off has_pages and the doc
template off has_pages / has_package_sources rather than has_docs.

Worth noting that has_package_sources (generate.py:168) is already
`bool(package_sources) and package_type == "doc"`, so the predicate needed for
the second half exists and is simply not the one used.

Found by an external review of the repository; both halves verified against the
code before filing. Not yet reproduced end to end -- the first task should be a
failing test that configures a package_sources-only doc package and asserts on
get_generated_files and on the rendered Makefile.
acceptance_criteria:
A doc package configured with package_sources and neither docs nor slides:

- get_generated_files lists the five shared page files, so `clean` removes them
  and the managed .gitignore section covers them.
- html-template.html is generated, so the `pkg` target's pandoc invocation names
  a template that exists.
- Both are covered by tests that fail if either predicate is changed back.

No behaviour change for packages that do declare docs or slides.
close_reason: get_generated_files now reads the derived context it already builds rather than re-spelling the predicates off raw config keys, and the doc template is injected for has_docs or has_package_sources. title: Regression test: a failed asset fails the PDF build instead of degrading it
description:
The generated pages are not self-contained. embed-images.lua inlines images, but Bootstrap, highlight.js, Mermaid and the webfonts are all fetched from CDNs when the page loads. A dropped request does not stop rendering -- it produces a finished-looking PDF with no diagrams, no syntax highlighting and fallback fonts.

html-to-pdf.js collects requestfailed, HTTP >= 400 and pageerror events and refuses to write the file, matching the --fail-if-warnings stance the pandoc services take. It checks twice on purpose: once right after load and once before printing. Mermaid is itself a CDN import, so a dead CDN means __mermaidReady never gets set, and checking only at the end would report a 120s timeout instead of the actual cause.

Both the refusal and the early check should be tested; the early check is easy to lose in a refactor and its absence only shows up as a slow, confusing failure.
acceptance_criteria: A test points the converter at an HTML file with an unresolvable asset reference and asserts a non-zero exit, no PDF on disk, and the failed URL named in stderr. A second assertion covers the fail-fast path: the failure is reported without waiting out the ready-flag timeout.
close_reason: PDF integration tests added. Geometry verified sensitive to the @page rules; fail-fast verified by removing the early check (122s vs 3s). Two findings recorded in the PR: preferCSSPageSize removal does not change output on current Chromium, and networkidle0 alone can satisfy the mermaid tests, so both are additionally asserted as template text.

title: Regression test: the PDF waits for client-side rendering before printing
description:
Mermaid renders in the browser, and _page-scripts.html.j2 only assembles the Bootstrap tab panes after dispatching mermaid-ready. html-to-pdf.js waits on window.__mermaidReady to avoid printing the page mid-build.

Two failure modes, neither visible in the HTML:

1. If the wait is removed, a PDF captures raw mermaid source sitting in a code block and tab content that never got moved into its pane. The HTML is still perfect; only the PDF is wrong.
2. If _page-scripts.html.j2 stops setting the flag, every PDF build hangs for the full 120s timeout instead of failing usefully.

The second is the reason the flag deserves a test rather than a comment: it is a contract between two templates that no build step checks.
acceptance_criteria: A test renders a fixture containing a mermaid diagram and a tabbed section to PDF, then asserts the extracted text contains the diagram's node labels and not its 'graph LR' source, and that content from every tab is present.
close_reason: PDF integration tests added. Geometry verified sensitive to the @page rules; fail-fast verified by removing the early check (122s vs 3s). Two findings recorded in the PR: preferCSSPageSize removal does not change output on current Chromium, and networkidle0 alone can satisfy the mermaid tests, so both are additionally asserted as template text.

title: Regression test: PDF page geometry comes from the print stylesheet
description:
html-to-pdf.js prints with preferCSSPageSize, so the @page rules in _page-style.css.j2 and _slide-style.css.j2 are the page geometry -- not a hint, and not something the browser overrides. Documents must come out letter portrait with 1in margins; decks must come out letter landscape with exactly one slide per page.

Nothing enforces this. Drop preferCSSPageSize, or edit an @page block, and the PDFs silently repaginate: a deck can fold two slides onto a page or spill one across two, and neither the build nor the HTML output changes at all.

This is an integration test -- it needs the container, unlike the argv assertions -- so it belongs behind the same marker used for the pandoc build tests.
acceptance_criteria: A test renders a fixture document and deck to PDF and asserts page count and MediaBox: 612x792 for the document, 792x612 for the deck with one page per slide plus the title slide. Fails if preferCSSPageSize is removed from page.pdf().
close_reason: PDF integration tests added. Geometry verified sensitive to the @page rules; fail-fast verified by removing the early check (122s vs 3s). Two findings recorded in the PR: preferCSSPageSize removal does not change output on current Chromium, and networkidle0 alone can satisfy the mermaid tests, so both are additionally asserted as template text.

title: Template test: the pdf target wires OUTPUT_SUFFIX and its dependencies correctly
description:
Docker-free counterpart to the pandoc argv tests: assert on the rendered Makefile text rather than on a build.

Three contracts, all currently defended by nothing:

1. $(OUTPUT_SUFFIX) appears on BOTH sides of each pdf conversion. If it is dropped from one side, 'make pdf with=hidden' prints the plain HTML into the -hidden PDF, or the -hidden HTML into the plain one. The output looks fine; it is just the wrong document, which is the worst possible failure for an answer-key build.
2. pdf depends on doc, so a PDF is never printed from stale HTML left over from a previous run.
3. clean-pkg removes the .pdf and -*.pdf globs alongside the .html ones.

Also worth asserting that the pdf target exists for any package with docs or slides and is absent otherwise, since it is gated on has_pages with no config key.
acceptance_criteria: A test renders Makefile.j2 for a package with both docs and slides and asserts the pdf recipe pairs matching suffixes, depends on doc, and that clean-pkg covers the pdf globs. Fails if OUTPUT_SUFFIX is removed from either side.
close_reason: Ten Docker-free tests on the rendered Makefile: OUTPUT_SUFFIX paired on both sides of every conversion, pdf depends on doc, doc depends on slide, clean-pkg covers the pdf globs, pdf is phony, and the has_pages gate across all four docs/slides combinations. Mutation-verified per the acceptance criteria.

title: config.example.yaml documents the removed LaTeX PDF pipeline
description:
The PDF pandoc/LaTeX pipeline was deleted in 'Replace PDF output with HTML document generation', but stencil/config.example.yaml was never updated. It still lists pandoc-header.tex.j2, pandoc-template.latex.j2, and Dockerfile.pdf.j2 in its templates block -- three files that no longer exist in stencil/templates/. It also documents 'has_pdfs' as an available when-condition, describes package_type as "zip" or "pdf" when generate.py validates against (doc, zip, none), documents a 'pdfs:' package field that generate.py does not read, and sets 'pdfs: [README.md]' on the example workspace package.

This is a live bug rather than mere staleness: copying the example config and running 'stencil gen' fails on the first missing template.

Scope: remove every LaTeX/PDF reference from the example config so it describes only what the code implements. Do not touch the print CSS in _page-style.css.j2 / _slide-style.css.j2 or the Printing sections of STENCIL.md and AUTHORING.md -- those are the browser print path and are intentional.
acceptance_criteria: stencil/config.example.yaml contains no reference to pandoc-header.tex.j2, pandoc-template.latex.j2, Dockerfile.pdf.j2, has_pdfs, pdfs, or package_type: pdf. Copying the example config into a scratch directory and running 'stencil gen workspace' succeeds. Change lands via a pull request, not a direct commit to main.

title: Guard the template pipeline with executable tests
description:
stencil has no tests, no CI and no test dependencies, across 84 commits and seven months. Every check performed while shipping the authoring-contract epic was manual and thrown away.

That matters most for two ordering constraints in stencil/templates/docker-compose-html.yml.j2 defended by nothing but a code comment:

  1. --citeproc must follow --lua-filter=hidden-filter.lua. Reorder it and works cited only inside `::: {.hidden}` appear in the reference list of the build that drops the hidden content. The answer key's sources leak, silently, into a handout.
  2. For decks, --citeproc must precede --lua-filter=slide-sections.lua. Reorder it and the reference list renders at div.container.deck > div#refs, outside every slide card, where present mode never displays it.

Both were reproduced during the original work. Neither would be caught today.

The history also shows why this is worth doing: the Mermaid id-collision bug took four passes to fix and the tabs epic reopened twice over six months. Those are regressions a golden-file suite catches on the first pass.
notes:
Scope extended after the PDF work landed (PRs #7 and #8). This epic was written before 'make pdf' existed, so its original seven tasks cover only the pandoc stage. Four tasks added for the PDF stage: stn-rxn.8 (Docker-free, asserts the Makefile wiring), and stn-rxn.9/.10/.11 (integration, need the container).

The PDF stage has the same shape of risk the epic was created for -- contracts defended by comments, with silent failure modes. Its geometry lives in the print CSS, its correctness depends on a window.__mermaidReady flag set by a different template, and its assets come from CDNs at load time. All of it was verified by hand and thrown away, which is the exact complaint in this description.

title: The decision journal keys three different tickets into one file
description:
Found while flushing stn-k73's journal.

/Users/wgrim/.claude/foundry/journals/run-7857ebf5bee1.jsonl holds 307 entries spanning THREE epics:

    epic values in that one file: {None: 183, '(unset)': 76, 'stn-bd3': 23, 'stn-3c9': 18, 'stn-ox1': 7}
    ticket pointers: {'stn-bd3.10': 4, 'stn-3c9.4': 1}

stn-3c9 is stn-38o's epic, worked in a different worktree and a different session; stn-bd3 is older still. They should not share a run id with stn-k73's session, and the run id is supposed to be derived from $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID via 'decision-journal run-id --key'.

The visible consequence: 'flush --epic stn-ox1' resolved its create-or-claim target to stn-3c9.4 -- ANOTHER epic's decision ticket -- and refused, because a flush REPLACES the design field and writing there would have destroyed stn-38o's decision log. The refusal is the tool working correctly; the shared journal is the bug. Worked around by creating stn-ox1.5 by hand and passing 'flush --ticket stn-ox1.5'.

Two things to investigate:
- why several sessions resolve to one run id (either run-id's key derivation, or the PreToolUse hook journaling under a key that is not the session's)
- whether 'flush' should scope its create-or-claim to entries matching --epic rather than to the journal's most recent ticket pointer, which is what made another epic's ticket the target

The 183 entries with epic None and 76 with '(unset)' are the same story from the other side: entries recorded before an epic existed cannot be flushed anywhere, which is the failure mode ticket-ship-pr's own Decision Journal Setup section warns about.
notes: Root cause confirmed 2026-09-09: the three epics were three ticket-ship-pr subagents of ONE session, and subagents inherit the parent's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, so run-id keyed correctly and they still shared a journal; cmd_flush reads every entry with no epic filter. Fix is being made in foundry as foundry-7g1 (attribution rule: unset entries belong to the most recently claimed epic before them; flush/render/status scope to --epic).

title: A global --config before the subcommand is silently ignored
description:
Found by the CodeRabbit gate on stn-k73's PR, and CONFIRMED by running it. PRE-EXISTING.

main() adds --config and --dry-run to the top-level parser AND, via _add_global_opts, to every subparser with the same defaults. argparse applies the subparser's default AFTER the main parser has stored the real value, so the default overwrites it:

    $ stencil --config other.yaml list
    Error: no config file at .../$PWD/.config.yaml      # other.yaml ignored
    $ stencil list --config other.yaml
    Available packages:  hs1 ...                          # works

The BROKEN order is the documented one. generate.py's own module docstring reads:

    stencil [--config <path>] gen [--all] [pkg]

so anyone following the usage string gets the wrong file read, with an error that names a file they did not ask for -- or, worse, a SUCCESSFUL run against the wrong config.

Fix: pass default=argparse.SUPPRESS for the duplicated options in _add_global_opts, so an unsupplied subparser option leaves the main parser's parsed value in place. Needs a test matrix over both argument orders across gen/clean/install/list, which is why it was not folded into stn-k73.

Deliberately NOT fixed in stn-k73: that ticket's approved boundary had three objectives, all about config errors failing closed. 'The CLI reads a different file than the one you named' is a distinct failure, and adding it at the review stage would have grown an operator-approved scope by a fourth objective at the last minute. Related: stn-k73's aggregated error message deliberately names no file BECAUSE --config means the path is not always .config.yaml -- which is only half true until this is fixed.

title: A symlinked brand: copies under a name clean cannot see and git tracks
description:
Found by the adversarial code review of stn-k73 (PR for epic stn-ox1), REPRODUCED end to end. PRE-EXISTING; not introduced by that change.

copy_brand_image names the destination '(config_dir / relative).resolve().name' -- .resolve() follows symlinks. get_generated_files names the same file 'Path(brand_image).name', from the raw config string. Two spellings of one rule, and they diverge on a symlink:

    ln -s img/siu-logo-2024.svg logo.svg     # brand: file://logo.svg
    stencil gen --all   ->  out/demo/siu-logo-2024.svg
    get_generated_files ->  ['demo/logo.svg']
    stencil clean --all ->  siu-logo-2024.svg SURVIVES

So the copied logo is absent from the managed .gitignore section and survives clean --all. That is exactly stn-k73's failure mode -- a generated file that is neither ignored nor cleaned -- reached by a different route, which is why it is worth its own ticket rather than a footnote.

Fix: make the destination basename come from ONE place. Cheapest is to stop resolving in copy_brand_image (destination = output_dir / Path(relative).name), so the copied name is always the configured name. If following the symlink is deliberate, brand_problem should return the resolved basename and get_generated_files should use that.

Left out of stn-k73 deliberately: copy_brand_image's destination naming was not in that ticket's objectives, the fix changes an output filename (a compatibility question), and it needs its own test.

title: read_lockfile's ValueError is reported as a broken config
description:
Found by the adversarial code review of stn-k73 (PR for epic stn-ox1), and REPRODUCED against a corrupted vendored file.

pipeline.read_lockfile raises FileNotFoundError when a vendored lockfile is missing (which correctly escapes stencil's config pre-flight as a traceback) and ValueError when it does not end in exactly one newline. get_template_context calls it, so that ValueError is collected by package_contexts and reported as a config problem:

    Error: the config has this problem:
    - browser-package-lock.json must end with exactly one newline; npm writes it that way, ...

    Nothing was generated, removed or written. Fix the config and run again -- and if
    files from an earlier, working config are still on disk, remove that directory by
    hand instead of ...

The config is fine. The real fix is 'python3 scripts/vendor_npm_locks.py'. The message sends the user to edit .config.yaml and to rm -rf a generated directory by hand -- wrong advice for the right failure.

Not fixed in stn-k73 because stencil/pipeline.py was outside that ticket's approved boundary. The clean fix is for read_lockfile to raise a distinct type for 'this install is not vendored correctly' -- the same failure class as the FileNotFoundError two lines above it, so arguably one type for both -- which generate.py's pre-flight then does not catch. A comment in package_contexts records the gap and points here.

title: gen --all still exits 0 when a template fails to render or a package has no templates
description:
Found by the adversarial review of stn-k73 (epic stn-ox1). Adjacent to that ticket's fail-open class but NOT closed by it -- stn-k73 closes the config-error path only.

Two paths survive it:
- render_templates re-raises (generate.py ~line 1003) and nothing in main catches it, so a StrictUndefined error is still a raw traceback AND still leaves a half-written package on disk.
- generate_package's 'if not template_defs: print(...); return None' (~line 944) lets the --all loop continue and main return with exit 0.

Both are near-dead in practice today, which is why stn-k73's CHANGELOG bullet is worded 'config errors fail the build' rather than 'a broken package fails the build'. Closing these would make the stronger claim true.

title: package 'dir' is never validated yet prefixes every path clean deletes
description:
Found by the adversarial review of stn-k73 (epic stn-ox1). PRE-EXISTING, out of scope there.

package.get('dir', package_id) is never run through check_config_path, yet it prefixes every entry get_generated_files returns -- which is every line of the managed .gitignore section AND every path clean_generated deletes. 'dir: ../..' reaches (output_base / entry).resolve() and deletes outside output_base.

Filed because stn-k73 makes stencil tell a 'the config is checked now' story, and this is the loudest remaining place where it is not. Same fix shape as the brand ticket: check_config_path, or a containment check before deletion.

title: brand is the one config path never checked, and copy_brand_image copies a symlink's target into a handed-over folder
description:
Found by the adversarial review of stn-k73 (epic stn-ox1). PRE-EXISTING and deliberately NOT fixed there -- copy_brand_image's body is outside that ticket's objectives.

Every other configured path goes through check_config_path. `brand` does not. Measured through brand_image_path:

  '../../../../etc/passwd.png'  -> '../../../../etc/passwd.png'
  '/var/root/secret.png'        -> '/var/root/secret.png'
  'file:///etc/hosts.svg'       -> '/etc/hosts.svg'

(config_dir / relative).resolve() with an absolute relative yields the absolute path.

The part that matters is not path traversal but CONTENT. copy_brand_image does shutil.copyfile on the RESOLVED path, so a symlink named logo.png pointing at any readable file copies that file's CONTENT into the generated package -- a folder AGENTS.md says is 'routinely handed to someone as a project of their own'. Only the suffix has to look like an image; the content is never checked. That is a content-exfiltration primitive into a distributed artifact.

Not a privilege boundary (whoever writes .config.yaml can already run anything via pre_build.run when someone runs make) -- but note stencil itself never executes that, so a CI job running only 'stencil gen --dry-run' over a PR branch's config gets no execution today and would get this.

Fix to consider: run brand through check_config_path, or at minimum an is_relative_to(config_dir) containment check on the resolved source.

description:

- the quoted-show_download sentence (~line 209) gains the same reach

CHANGELOG.md:

- Say what changed and why it is a fail-closed decision, in the voice the rest of the file uses.

notes:
## AMENDMENTS from the Phase 4 reviews

1. **Document the collective behaviour in STENCIL.md** (decision d-adf7c52b):
   a config error in ANY package fails `gen`, `install` and `clean` -- including
   single-package `gen <pkg>` and `clean <pkg>`. Both reviewers said that if this
   is not written down the next contributor will "fix" it as a bug. Say why:
   validate_config already gated single-package gen on global custom-key errors,
   so this extends an existing contract.

2. **Say that the brand FILE-EXISTENCE check is gen-only** (d-96da97d8), and why:
   the .gitignore entry and the clean list derive from the brand string, not the
   file, so the check buys install and clean nothing and would only stop `clean`
   from recovering. The brand-alt check DOES run everywhere. The STENCIL.md
   brand-alt row (~line 248) needs both halves, not just "stencil gen fails".

3. **The CHANGELOG bullet says "config errors fail the build", NOT "a broken
   package fails the build".** The stronger claim is not yet true -- a template
   that fails to render still tracebacks and still leaves a half-written package,
   and a package with no templates still lets `gen --all` exit 0. Both are filed
   as stn-zfc. stn-ox1.3's own acceptance is "no claim in either file that the
   code does not do", and this is that claim.

4. **Correct the acceptance wording inherited from the epic.** "The managed
   .gitignore section is not written at all rather than written incomplete" is
   only true on the CREATE path. On the UPDATE path an abort leaves the OLD
   section intact -- which is the safe direction (a stale section is a superset
   for every package that was already fine, so it over-ignores; a truncated one
   under-ignores and silently makes a build product committable). Word it as
   "the managed section is never replaced by a truncated one".

title: Implement: aggregated fail-closed pre-flight in generate.py
description:

Files: stencil/generate.py ONLY.

5. install_gitignore(config, dry_run=False, config_dir=None) and clean_generated(output_base, config, package_id=None, dry_run=False, config_dir=None) -- thread config_dir through. OPTIONAL and LAST, so existing positional call sites in tests keep working.
6. main -- pass config_dir to install and clean, and wrap both branches in 'except ValueError as e: print(f"Error: {e}", file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(1)', matching what the gen branch already does around validate_config. gen needs NO new handler: validate_config runs before the --all loop.

Aggregate rather than first-error-wins. That is what the existing line-709 comment ('a config error in one should not hide a naming error in another') was protecting, and it must survive the move to failing closed.

Do NOT refactor get_template_context. Do NOT touch stencil/templates/, pipeline.py, assets.py, or stencil/__init__.py (no version bump).

the command it was written about: the pre-flight would run brand_problem with
no filesystem root, skip the existence half, let render_templates write every
file, and then copy_brand_image (line 952, OUTSIDE generate_package's try)
throws a raw traceback over a half-generated directory -- verbatim the defect
objective 3 exists to close.

    validate_config(config: dict, env: Environment, config_dir: Path | None = None)

passes config_dir through to the pre-flight; main line ~1342 becomes
`validate_config(config, env, config_dir)`, where config_dir is already in
scope (line ~1287). tests/test_config_validation.py:43 calls it with two
positional args, so the optional third is safe.

**A2 -- the existence check is gen-only. get_generated_files,
install_gitignore and clean_generated gain NOTHING; leave all three
signatures exactly as they are.** This REPLACES plan step 5. Reason recorded
as decision d-96da97d8: the .gitignore entry and the clean list both derive
from the brand STRING (line ~1055), not from the file, so a missing brand file
cannot make either list short -- the check buys install and clean no
fail-closed value and only adds a way for `clean`, a recovery operation, to
refuse. The rule to write into the comment: fail closed on what the config
SAYS (deterministic, machine-independent); check what the filesystem HAS only
where stencil is about to depend on it.

install and clean still fail closed on every config error, including a missing
brand-alt. Only the file-existence half is gen-only.

**A3 -- collect more than ValueError, and guard the shapes.** get_template_context
line ~201 does `config.get("packages", {}).get(package_id)` and line ~205 does
`package.get(...)`, so `packages:` as a LIST and a package whose value is a
STRING both raise AttributeError, not ValueError -- a raw traceback from
exactly the malformed config this pre-flight exists to report. Also `docs: 5`
(TypeError), `output_dir: 5` (TypeError), `brand: 5` (AttributeError).

  (a) Reject a non-mapping config["packages"], and a non-mapping package value,
      with a clear ValueError naming the offender. load_config (line ~60) sets
      the precedent for the message style.
  (b) Collect `(ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError, KeyError)` and include
      `type(e).__name__` in the collected line, so a genuine stencil bug stays
      distinguishable from a config error rather than being laundered into one.

  Do NOT catch bare Exception: pipeline.read_lockfile raises
  FileNotFoundError/ValueError for a broken INSTALL, and that must not be
  reported as a config error in every package at once.

**A4 -- gate brand_problem on has_pages.** copy_brand_image is called only under
`if context.get("has_pages")` (line ~950) and get_generated_files gates its
brand entry the same way (line ~1052). Ungated, a page-less package
(package_type: none, no docs/slides) inheriting a config-level image brand with
no brand-alt would NEWLY fail gen/install/clean -- and because config-level
brands are inherited, one missing brand-alt at the top level would name every
page-less package at once. Call brand_problem only when the just-computed
context["has_pages"] is true; the context is right there, so this costs nothing.

**A5 -- define the both-broken interaction.** When get_template_context raised
for a package: record that message and `continue`. Do NOT then call
brand_problem for it -- there is no context to read has_pages from, and a
non-mapping package value would explode inside the collector itself.

**A6 -- preserve the two message substrings.** brand_problem's returned strings
must keep the literal substrings `brand-alt` and `not a file`:
tests/test_brand.py's `pytest.raises(match=...)` regexes are substring
searches, and those two tests are what prove copy_brand_image still raises for
the direct generate_package API that conftest.make_package uses. Preserve
copy_brand_image's early short-circuit too -- brand_image_path() returning None
means return None BEFORE the alt check, so a plain-name brand and a remote URL
are still fine with no alt.

**A7 -- move the stale comment.** The aggregation rationale at lines ~706-708
("a config error in one should not hide a naming error in another") is the
reason the pre-flight aggregates; move it onto the new function. Update
validate_config's docstring, which will no longer describe what it does.

## AMENDMENTS from the Phase 4 adversarial review (second pass)

**B1 -- keep main's `try` NARROW. Do not wrap the whole install/clean branch.**
This REPLACES the wording of plan step 6. `clean_generated` unlinks files in a
loop and then rmdirs; a broad `except ValueError` there would print a bare
`Error: <msg>` with the traceback suppressed AFTER an unknown number of files
were already deleted. Suppressing a traceback is right for "your config is
wrong" and WRONG for "something failed halfway through destroying files". The
gen branch already does this correctly -- its try at line ~1338 wraps
`validate_config(config, env)` and nothing else. Mirror that: call the
validation explicitly and narrowly, catch around THAT call only, then run
install_gitignore / clean_generated outside the try.

**B2 -- escape control characters in the aggregated message.** The interpolations
in generate.py are raw, no `!r`: `{package_id}` everywhere, `{package_type}`
(:220), `{package['package_folder']}` (:236), brand `{value}` (:795, :806),
`{', '.join(clashes)}` (:545). A package id or brand value containing `\r` or
`\x1b[1A\x1b[2K` erases previously-printed lines of the report -- defeating
the exact "one error cannot hide another" guarantee this PR sells, while the
aggregation test still passes because it asserts on the Python string and the
terminal renders something else. Also a CI-log integrity issue. Escape each
collected problem as it goes into the aggregate:

    def _safe(text: str) -> str:
        """Config-supplied text is data, not terminal control."""
        return "".join(
            c if c == "\n" or c == " " or c.isprintable() else repr(c)[1:-1]
            for c in str(text)
        )

Note `check_config_path` and `show_download_default` already use `{text!r}` /
`{value!r}` and are safe -- do not change them.

**B3 -- dedupe identical problems.** `show_download_default` checks package scope
then CONFIG scope and raises with where="config"; `reject_derived("config-level",
...)` runs inside every package's context build; a config-level brand with no
brand-alt fails for every package via brand_of's fallback. So ONE top-level typo
produces one identical line per package -- 200 packages, 200 identical lines,
and the real per-package errors scroll off. Dedupe the collected strings
(`dict.fromkeys` preserves order) before building the message.

**B4 -- brand_problem's config_dir must be positional-required.** An optional
`config_dir=None` that silently skips half the check is the same shape of defect
this PR removes: three call sites must remember to pass it and forgetting is
silent. Make it `brand_problem(package, config, config_dir)` -- callers with no
root pass an explicit `None`. The PUBLIC get_generated_files /
install_gitignore / clean_generated params stay optional-and-last for the
positional call sites in tests; that part is unaffected (and per d-96da97d8
those three gain no parameter at all).

**B5 -- get_generated_files must CONSUME the returned contexts.** It must not
call the pre-flight and then keep its own get_template_context loop -- that
would take install/clean from N context builds to 2N. Consuming them is the
only reason the pre-flight returns them.

**B6 -- reorder clean's unknown-package check.** After this change
`clean <unknown-pkg>` on a config that ALSO has a broken package reports the
config error instead of "Unknown package", because get_generated_files
(line ~1093) now precedes the membership check (line ~1099). Move the
membership check ahead of the entries computation.

**B7 -- the error message names the escape hatch.** `clean` becomes unavailable
exactly when it is most wanted: config drifted, generated files on disk. Failing
closed is still right (deleting from a misread config is worse), but the message
must say the way out -- fix the config, or remove the directory by hand --
or the first person to hit it reaches for a wider `rm -rf` than they meant.

**B8 -- collective failure is DECIDED (d-adf7c52b): every command, all packages.**
`gen <pkg>` and `clean <pkg>` fail when a DIFFERENT package is broken. This is
deliberate, not a side effect: validate_config already gates single-package gen
on global template_env/when: errors today, so this extends an existing contract
rather than inventing one. Document it in STENCIL.md (stn-ox1.3) and pin it with
a test (stn-ox1.4).

**B9 -- correct the aggregation justification, do not repeat mine.** My plan
claimed the line-706 comment's intent "survives the move to failing closed".
That is only half true and the comment must not say otherwise: aggregation
preserves it WITHIN the class of package errors, but the `when:` and unread
`template_env` checks now sit BEHIND the pre-flight and are deferred by one
round. That is deliberate -- you cannot report "Known keys:" from a config you
cannot read, and today's answer is computed from a silently truncated set --
but write it honestly on the new function rather than claiming nothing was lost.
close_reason: Implemented and reviewed. Four corrections in review: a misattribution bug that blamed a valid package for a malformed sibling (shape now checked in its own pass, since get_template_context reads every package via declared_template_env_keys); dropped the 'ValueError: ' prefix from ordinary config messages, keeping class names only on unexpected types where they mean something; rewrote the lead line, which read 'Error: Config is broken:' and named .config.yaml even under --config; and switched main's pre-flight from get_generated_files to package_contexts so the call says what it is for. 803 passed before rebase, 849 after.

title: Pin pandoc's YAML boolean resolution in a test
description:
Write tests/test_yaml_resolution.py (NEW FILE).

Files: tests/test_yaml_resolution.py

An integration-marked module that OWNS the measurement three prose sites
currently restate from memory. It writes a probe Lua filter and a front matter
block covering every spelling, drives them through pipeline.PANDOC_IMAGE
directly (NOT pipeline.render -- its argv is fixed and runs the whole template
chain), and asserts the measured table.

REUSE pipeline.container_runtime() and pipeline.PANDOC_IMAGE. Do not invent a
third way to find docker/podman. pipeline.py itself is on the deny list, so the
few lines of docker-run argv are duplicated deliberately rather than by
refactoring the render harness.

MEASURED against pandoc 3.10.0.0 -- pandoc resolves exactly YAML 1.1's
ENUMERATED boolean forms, which means three casings and no others:

  boolean:      y Y yes Yes YES  n N no No NO
                on On ON  off Off OFF
                true True TRUE  false False FALSE
  MetaString '': null Null NULL, ~, and a blank value (all indistinguishable)
  nil:          the key absent
  MetaInlines:  EVERYTHING ELSE, including
                  - mixed case: nO yEs yeS ofF oN tRue falsE nUll
                  - numbers and words: 1 0 2 none
                  - anything quoted: "no" "null" ""

'(any case)' IS WRONG and must not be repeated -- it is one of the claims this
ticket exists to correct. Stencil still behaves correctly for mixed case only
because truthy() lowercases before consulting the FALSE table, which is a
better reason for that table to exist than the ticket gives.

The probe reports type(v), pandoc.utils.type(v) and pandoc.utils.stringify(v)
per key, prints a marker-prefixed JSON line, and the test json.loads it -- the
shape tests/test_download.py uses for its browser probe.

NOTE: this is a characterization pin, not a red-green test. It passes on the
first run because pandoc already behaves this way; its job is to FAIL on a
future image bump that flips resolution. Say that in the docstring rather than
pretending it drove the implementation.

Acceptance: passes under a real pandoc container; a deliberately wrong expected
value fails with a message naming the key and the type; the module cannot pass
by measuring nothing.
close_reason: tests/test_yaml_resolution.py pins all 43 spellings; both mutations independently reproduced

title: A bad config value silently drops a package instead of failing the build
description:
Found by the adversarial code review of stn-ejv (epic stn-bd3). PRE-EXISTING and not caused by that change; deliberately not fixed there.

show_download_default() raises ValueError on a non-boolean config value, and that raise reaches two call sites that swallow ValueError and `continue`:
- the `when:` key validator (around stencil/generate.py line 703)
- the `stencil install` gitignore builder (around line 1135)

So a quoted "no" in .config.yaml does NOT fail the build. It silently drops that package from the managed gitignore section, which then goes stale without saying so.

The fail-open is general: it applies to EVERY config error those two paths can hit, not just show_download. The new key only widened the set of ways to trip it. That is why this is its own ticket rather than a change inside stn-ejv's boundary -- fixing it means deciding what those two call sites should do with a genuinely broken config, which is a question about the whole config surface.

Worth checking whether the same swallow hides errors from check_config_path and brand validation too.
notes:
## Design decision (operator, 2026-09-08): fail closed, aggregated pre-flight

The ticket's open question -- what the two swallowing call sites should do with
a genuinely broken config -- is settled as **option B**.

Investigation found three defects, not two, plus an answer to the ticket's
"worth checking" note:

- `validate_config` (line ~709) and `get_generated_files` (line ~1035) both
  swallow every ValueError `get_template_context` raises. That hides
  package_type, package_sources, the package_folder rename, pre_build naming
  and collisions, output_dir, template_env derived-key clashes, and
  check_config_path (shell metacharacters, whitespace, ~, absolute, ..) --
  not only show_download.
- Reproduced: `stencil install` exits 0 with the broken package absent from
  the managed .gitignore section and nothing on stderr; `stencil clean --all`
  exits 0 having cleaned only the good packages; `stencil gen --all` exits 0
  after printing the error to stderr, so a Makefile or CI step sees success.
- check_config_path IS hidden by the swallow. Brand validation is NOT -- but
  it has the mirror-image defect: `copy_brand_image` raises outside
  `generate_package`'s try/except, so a missing `brand-alt` escapes as a raw
  Python traceback AFTER the package has been half-generated, which
  contradicts tests/test_cli.py's stated contract.

Decision: one aggregated pre-flight that reads every package's context and
validates the brand pair, raising a single named, traceback-free report that
lists EVERY broken package at once, before anything is written. `install`,
`clean` and `gen` all fail closed with a non-zero exit.

Aggregating rather than first-error-wins preserves what the line 709 comment
was actually protecting ("a config error in one should not hide a naming error
in another") while failing closed. `gen --all`'s exit-0 closes as a
consequence, since validate_config already runs before that loop.

Rejected: (A) leaving the brand traceback to a follow-up bead -- it would sit
directly beside the new fail-closed pre-flight; (C) merely catching the brand
error in generate_package -- kills the traceback but still leaves a

````text
### M1. The aggregation guarantee is defeatable by a control character, and the test that "proves" it would not notice

You asked whether terminal escape injection is real here given `pre_build.run` is arbitrary execution. Two things make it worth a small fix rather than a shrug:

**(a) The premise is weaker than it looks.** `stencil` never invokes pandoc (AGENTS.md, first line of Architecture). `pre_build.run` is *interpolated into a generated Makefile*; it executes when someone runs `make`. A CI job that runs only `stencil install` or `stencil gen --dry-run` over a config from a PR branch gets **no** command execution from stencil today. So "whoever writes .config.yaml can already run anything" is true of the *build*, not of the *generator*. The comment above `_UNSAFE_IN_PATH` is careful to say this is not a privilege boundary — agreed, and I am not claiming one.

**(b) The concrete harm is to the invariant this PR exists to create.** These interpolations are raw, no `!r`:

- `f"Package {package_id} is missing required 'package_type'"` (:227) — and every other `{package_id}` in the file
- `f"Package {package_id} has invalid package_type: {package_type}"` (:220)
- `f"package_sources: [{package['package_folder']}]"` (:236)
- `f"brand is an image ({value}) but brand-alt is not set"` (:795) and `f"brand points at {value}"` (:806)
- `f"…may not redefine …: {', '.join(clashes)}"` (:545)
- `f"Known keys: {', '.join(sorted(available))}"` (:717)

`check_config_path` and `show_download_default` use `{text!r}` / `{value!r}`, which Python escapes (`repr("\x1b[2J")` → `'\\x1b[2J'`) — those are already safe. The raw ones are not. A package id or brand value containing `\r` or `\x1b[1A\x1b[2K` erases previously-printed lines of the aggregated report. That is *literally* the guarantee the plan sells and stn-ox1.1 tests: "TWO broken packages produce ONE message naming BOTH… this is the test that catches a regression to first-error-wins." That test asserts on the Python string; the terminal renders something else. It is also a CI-log integrity issue (`\x1b[32mAll packages OK\x1b[0m` inside a package id).

**Fix.** One line in the message builder, where you are already formatting:

```python
def _safe(text: str) -> str:
    """Config-supplied text is data, not terminal control."""
    return "".join(c if c == "\n" or (c.isprintable() or c == " ") else repr(c)[1:-1]
                   for c in str(text))
```

Apply it to each collected problem in `preflight_config`. Cheap, local to new code, and it makes the aggregation test's claim true of the thing the reader actually sees. Add a test with `\x1b[1A` in a package id.

Related, lower: `_UNSAFE_IN_PATH` (`[$\`;|&<>\\\n]`) plus the `isspace()` check does not reject ESC or other C0 controls — `\x1b` is neither in the class nor whitespace — so they reach the generated Makefile. Harmless to `/bin/sh`, but it is the same class and worth one bead.

### L2. Was the swallow load-bearing? Yes, in one place worth naming

`stencil clean` becomes unavailable exactly when you most want it: the config drifted, generated files are on disk, and now you cannot remove them without first fixing the config. Chicken-and-egg. Failing closed is still the right call — deleting from a misread config is strictly worse than refusing — but the error message should say the escape hatch out loud ("fix the config, or remove `<output_base>/<dir>` by hand"), otherwise the first person to hit it will `rm -rf` something wider than they meant to.

**Stale-vs-truncated, both sides.** Truncated-new is worse. A stale section is a *superset* for every package that was already fine, so it over-ignores — the safe direction. Truncated-new under-ignores those same packages, so a build product that was ignored yesterday becomes committable today, *and* it does so silently. Both miss the broken package equally. The only argument for truncated-new is that a stale section can outlive a removed package and keep ignoring a path someone later wants tracked — a nuisance, not a data loss. | Parameter | Default | Meaning |
````
````text
|---|---|---|
| Poll interval | 30s | how often to check for new CodeRabbit activity |
| Quiet window | 10 min | no new activity this long after a push → clean |
| Hard timeout | 45 min | total wall-clock → stop and ask the user |
| Iteration ceiling | 10 | passes → stop and ask the user |
````

```text
## 2. `make pdf` fails hard on an undrawable glyph, and the plan specifies the glyph only as "a down-arrow"

`html-to-pdf.js.j2:212` collects `document.body.innerText`, measures every character against the `.notdef` width of the inlined font stack, and **throws** if any character has no glyph. It runs at line 1135, *before* `collectLinkText` switches to print emulation — so it runs in **screen** media, where the download button is visible. `display: none` under `@media print` does not protect it.

The theme toggle's `☀ ☾ ◐` pass today, which proves those three resolve in the container's font stack and nothing more. A plausible choice like U+2B73 (⭳), U+2913 (⤓) or U+21E9 (⇩) is not covered by Crimson Pro, Inter or JetBrains Mono, all of which are subset to latin + latin-ext. And because `show_download` now defaults to **true**, the failure is not scoped to opt-in pages: it breaks `make pdf` for every package of every consumer on upgrade, with the message "characters that no inlined font can draw".

**Fix:** name the glyph in stn-bd3.4 rather than leaving it to the implementer, and pick from what is already proven — U+2193 (↓) is the conservative choice, and it must be verified by running the PDF tier, not by reading the stylesheet. Consider adding the character to the assertion set in the new PDF test so the choice is pinned rather than incidental. The plan's own tier-4 PDF test will catch this, but only if it is written before the glyph is chosen, which the current task order does not guarantee.

## 3. The head capture costs ~2.4 MB per page, on every page, and buys almost nothing (concern 4)

Measured sizes in `stencil/assets/`: `fonts.css` is **2,117,225 bytes**, `bootstrap.min.css` 232,803, plus the highlight CSS. All of it is in `<head>`. So `document.head.innerHTML` on a *typical text-only handout* is about **2.4 MB before any author content**, retained for the life of the tab, on every generated page, by default.

That is the wrong place to spend it, because almost nothing mutates the head. I grepped every inlined bundle for `document.head`, `head.appendChild`, `getElementsByTagName('head')`: highlight.js — zero; Bootstrap — zero; Mermaid — one real site, cytoscape's `__________cytoscape_stylesheet` injection (`i.head` where `i = n.document`), which fires only for cytoscape-backed diagram types. Every head mutation in play is an **append**.

**Fix, and this is the strongest structural change I'd make to the plan:** do not capture the head as a string at all. Capture `document.head.childNodes.length` at parse time and, at click time, truncate the clone's head to that many children. That reverts every appended node, costs one integer, and eliminates the head reparse entirely — which also removes a whole injection surface from concern 1 for free. The cost is that it does not revert *modifications* to existing head nodes; nothing observed does that, and if something ever did, the string capture wouldn't have helped either unless the modification happened before the capture.

The container string is the one you genuinely cannot avoid, and holding it as a string is the right call over a detached clone — a detached `cloneNode(true)` of the container would carry per-node overhead *and*, as I measured, Chrome does live-load `<img>` in detached trees, so an image-heavy handout would decode every base64 image a second time. Say that in the changelog; it's the non-obvious part.

Sizing the residual risk honestly: a text handout's container is 50–200 KB, so ~2.4 MB total is nearly all head, and dropping the head capture makes the feature nearly free. An image-heavy handout with 15 MB of inlined base64 retains ~30 MB (V8 promotes the string to two-byte the moment the prose contains an em dash), and the click path transiently holds clone + assembled string + Blob on top of that — call it 3–4× document size at peak. That is uncomfortable on a Chromebook with a 30 MB deck and worth one measured test at a realistic ceiling, but it is not the everyday cost. **`make pdf` is not threatened**: the click never happens during a build, so the PDF path pays only the capture, and the compose file sets no container memory limit while `--disable-dev-shm-usage` is already passed.

## 4. Reverting body chrome by denylist is the fragile half of an otherwise good design

The "replace rather than strip" argument is correct and well made — hljs, mermaid and the tab builder *transform* rather than add, so node removal genuinely cannot undo them, and replacing `.container` reverts all three at once. That part I have no quarrel with.

What is fragile is what's left over. The plan names three things to undo outside the container: remove `.deck-toolbar`, empty `.theme-toggle-host`, drop two root attributes. That is a denylist of the chrome that exists in September 2026. It does not cover `<body>`'s own attributes (a Bootstrap component an author uses adds `class="modal-open"` and an inline `padding-right`), it does not cover a fourth widget added next release, and nothing fails when it goes stale — the download just quietly starts baking in whatever was added.

**Fix:** snapshot instead of denylist. At parse time record `document.body.childNodes.length` plus the body's and root's attribute name lists (three small arrays). At click time, truncate the clone's body to that count and remove any attribute not in the recorded set. Same amount of code, no names hardcoded, and the download button you add fifth is handled by construction. The `.deck-toolbar` test then passes for a reason that keeps holding.

Two smaller gaps in the same area:

- **`.container` may be absent.** `document.querySelector('.container').outerHTML` throws on a consumer who overrode `html-template.html.j2` and spelled the wrapper differently — and AGENTS.md documents that overriding the composition templates is a supported thing one consumer already does. An uncaught throw at parse time is a `pageerror`, which `html-to-pdf.js` turns into a failed build. The failure lands on *every* `make pdf` in that project, and it is the exact shape of the hljs-gate lesson already recorded in `_page-scripts.html.j2`. Guard the capture and, if it fails, do not mount the button at all — a missing button beats a broken build and beats a button that writes a corrupt file.
- **`mountDownloadButton` needs `mountThemeToggle`'s idempotency guard** (`if (container.querySelector('.download-button')) return;`) and must be allowed to return `undefined`, so `_slide-scripts.html.j2` can do `if (btn)` the way it already does for `themeGroup`.

## 5. The filename (concern 2): traversal is not reachable, but two other cases are, and one of them fails silently

I drove real blob downloads through `Browser.setDownloadBehavior` in the repo's Chromium and read the resulting directory:

| `a.download` value | file written |
|---|---|
| `../../../../tmp/evil.html` | `_.._.._.._tmp_evil.html` — nothing outside the download dir, `/tmp/evil.html` absent |
| `nul\u0000byte.html` | `nul_byte.html` |
| `rtl\u202Efdp.html` | `rtl_fdp.html` |
| `.html` | `html.html` |
| `""` | a UUID Chrome invented |
| 400 chars + `.html` | **nothing — `Browser.downloadProgress` reported `canceled`** |

So: **path traversal, the NUL byte and the RTL override are all neutralised by Chrome's own `download`-attribute sanitizer**, and on `file://` the vector is doubly unreachable — Chrome refuses to even navigate a `file://` URL containing `%2e%2e%2f` with `ERR_INVALID_URL`. In the stated threat model (a student opening a handout from disk) the traversal concern is theoretical, and I would not hold the PR for it.

The plan still has an ordering bug worth fixing on principle, because it costs nothing: it decodes *after* taking the basename, so a served URL like `https://host/%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2fetc%2fpasswd` yields the basename `%2e%2e%2f...` and `decodeURIComponent` reintroduces the separators. Decode first, then split on `/`, then sanitize.

The two cases that are genuinely reachable and are not defended by the browser:

- **An over-long name cancels the download with no error anywhere.** The click appears to do nothing. `location.pathname` basenames over ~255 bytes are unusual but entirely constructible on a served URL. Cap at ~200 characters.
- **An empty basename** — any directory-index URL, `https://host/course/` — gives `"" + ".html"` = `.html`, saved as `html.html`. The plan's fallback fires only when `decodeURIComponent` throws. Make it fire on an empty or dot-only stem too.

**Minimum sanitization I'd write:** decode inside try/catch → take everything after the last `/` → strip `[\u0000-\u001f\u007f]`, `[\\/:*?"<>|]` and the bidi controls `[\u202a-\u202e\u2066-\u2069]` → trim leading dots → if empty, `document` → append `.html` unless it already ends `.html`/`.htm` case-insensitively → cap at 200 chars. All of that is expressible without a `$` (character classes and `indexOf`/`slice`; only the `$` end-anchor is forbidden).

On the Blob: use `text/html;charset=utf-8`. The Blob constructor encodes the DOMString as UTF-8 and the captured head carries `<meta charset="UTF-8">`, so the two agree — that part is right. **Immediate `URL.revokeObjectURL` right after `a.click()` was safe** in Chrome across all eight of my downloads, so there is no leak provided the revoke actually runs; put it in a `finally` so a throw between `createObjectURL` and the revoke cannot pin a 30 MB blob for the life of the tab. Firefox and Safari are the engines that historically wanted a deferred revoke, and Safari from `file://` has a long history of ignoring `download` on blob URLs entirely — worth one sentence in AUTHORING.md rather than code.

## 6. Self-serialization as an injection surface (concern 1): I could not make it bite, and here is the evidence

I built a page containing the awkward cases and ran the plan's exact sequence — capture `.container.outerHTML`, `document.documentElement.cloneNode(true)`, `clone.querySelector('.container').outerHTML = captured` — twice.

- **The `outerHTML` setter on the detached clone works and does not throw.** The clone's `.container` has a parent (the cloned `<body>`), which is all the setter requires; only a null parent or a `Document` parent is a problem.
- **The operation is a fixed point.** Round 1 output equalled the capture exactly, and round 2 equalled round 1, for: `<noscript>` containing escaped markup, `<noscript>` containing live markup, `<template>` containing `<tr><td>`, inline SVG with `viewBox`, MathML, `<pre>` with a leading newline, `<textarea>`, and `&lt;script&gt;alert(1)&lt;/script&gt;` as text. Downloading a downloaded copy does not compound.
- **The `<noscript>` hazard specifically does not exist here.** I expected the fragment parser to run with scripting *disabled* (its document has no browsing context), which would reparse `&lt;b&gt;` into a real `<b>` and destroy the escaping. It does not — Chrome's fragment parser inherits scripting-enabled from the context document, and the child node types were identical (text, text) before and after. Raise this only against a design that uses `DOMParser`, which always parses with scripting disabled.
- **Scripts inserted via `innerHTML` on the clone do not run** (expected). **`<img onerror>` inserted the same way *does* run**, confirmed. That is a genuine detached-DOM sink, and it is worth knowing — but it is not an escalation here: the markup is the author's own, it already ran once when the page loaded, and the author controls the page absolutely. Not a finding.
- `<base>` and encoding declarations: the templates emit neither a `<base>` nor a second charset declaration, and the captured head carries the original `<meta charset="UTF-8">` forward. Nothing to attack.

One thing the plan should *not* claim: the download is **not** byte-identical to the built file. Measured drift on round 1: `&#160;` → `&nbsp;`, `&middot;` → literal `·`, `<path/>` → `<path></path>`, `<pre>\nfirst` → `<pre>first`. All semantically equivalent, all stable afterwards, and none of them disturb the non-breaking spaces that `_doc-body.html.j2` documents at length as load-bearing for the PDF text layer (they survive as `&nbsp;`). But the CHANGELOG and AUTHORING text drafted in stn-bd3.6 should say the button saves *a faithful copy of the page as built*, not *the file*, and no test should compare bytes.

---

## 7. Withheld content (concern 3): no new channel. Clean.

`hidden-filter.lua.j2` returns `{}` for a `.hidden` div — the content is deleted from the pandoc AST, at filter position 2 of the argv assembled in `stencil/pipeline.py:292`, before `--citeproc` and before the HTML writer ever runs. It never becomes markup, so there is nothing in the DOM for a serializer to find. The download partial captures `.container.outerHTML` from a document that already lacks it.

I checked the adjacent possibilities too. Decks have no presenter-notes feature (no `notes` rule anywhere in `_slide-style.css.j2`). Nothing is rendered-then-CSS-hidden except the visually-hidden accessible labels and the aria-hidden separators. `data-mermaid-source` and `data-caption` stash content that is already on the page. The tab builder hides panes at runtime, and the download restores the pre-builder markup — which is the built file, which the reader already has in full.

So the honest statement is: **the button exposes exactly nothing that Ctrl+S does not**, and that sentence belongs in AUTHORING.md, because it is the question the next reader of this feature will ask.

One policy note rather than a vulnerability: the instructor build (`--metadata include-hidden=true`) uses the same templates, so an answer-key HTML now ships with a one-click "save and send this to anyone" affordance. That does not make redistribution possible where it wasn't; it lowers the friction on the one artifact where friction was doing quiet work. Worth a line in AUTHORING.md recommending `show_download: false` on hidden-inclusive builds, or at minimum saying the key exists for that purpose.

## 8. Architecture: default-true has no package-level off switch

The operator's decision to default to true is what makes every finding above universal instead of opt-in, and the plan implements the default inside `frontmatter-filter.lua.j2` as a hardcoded Lua constant. A course with forty handouts that does not want the button must edit forty markdown files; there is no `.config.yaml` spelling, and `docker-compose-html.yml.j2` (where a `--metadata show_download=false` would go) is on the deny list for this run.

Every other cross-cutting knob in this repo is generation-time and lives where a consumer can reach it. Making the *default* a Jinja value — `truthy(meta.show_download, {{ show_download_default | tojson }})` resolved from config `template_env` — would cost one line and keep the operator's decision as the default while giving a package a way out. If that is out of scope for this PR, say so explicitly in the changelog, because the first consumer to ask will ask in an issue.

Related, and cheap: `html-template.html.j2` and `slide-template.html.j2` are precisely the files AGENTS.md says a consumer may override. A consumer on their own composition template gets `show_download: true` in metadata and no button, silently. The `_download.html.j2: set()` entry planned for `tests/test_template_contract.py` records that the partial reads nothing from the *Jinja* context, which is true and which guards nothing — the real new interface obligation is a *pandoc*-level one ("include this partial inside `$if(show_download)$`"), and that table cannot see it. Put it in the partial's own header comment where an overriding consumer will read it.

## 9. Smaller things, each with its fix

- **A deck with no slides gets no button at all.** `_slide-scripts.html.j2` early-returns on `slides.length === 0` before building the toolbar, and the deck template has no `.theme-toggle-host` for the document path to fall back to. `show_download: true` then does nothing, silently. Either accept and document it, or give the deck template the same host div.
- **The "no `$` anywhere" rule is stated with a wrong reason.** `$$` is pandoc's escape and `_page-scripts.html.j2` uses it deliberately (`/^\n|\n$$/g`, `/^H[1-6]$$/`). The convention is fine as a convention; the static test in stn-bd3.1 and its comment should say "this partial avoids `$` so no one has to reason about `$$` escaping", not "`$` starts a variable", which the neighbouring file disproves and which will mislead the next person who needs an end-anchor.
- **The CDP download test needs to poll the right thing.** Chrome writes a `.crdownload` partial first; poll `Browser.downloadProgress` for `state === 'completed'` (it is emitted, I saw it) rather than for a file appearing on disk. And note that under `setDownloadBehavior` a repeated filename **overwrites** — measured — so stn-bd3.3's "download from the downloaded copy" step will clobber the first file, since both derive the same name from `location.pathname`. Use two download directories, or read the first file before the second click.
- **WCAG 2.5.8 target size is not measured by the planned gate.** pa11y at WCAG 2.1 AA does not check target size; the deck's icon-only download button sitting beside the text-labelled Present button will be visibly narrower and may fall under 24×24. The plan's claim that "no deck stylesheet change is needed" is about contrast, which is right, and silent about size, which nothing in the test matrix will catch. Give it the same `min-width`/`min-height` the theme toggle's options already carry (`2rem`/`1.9rem`, `_page-style.css.j2:920`).
- **The document and deck buttons get different palettes** (`--text` on `--surface` in the document, `--on-accent` on `--accent-fill` inherited from `.deck-toolbar button` in a deck). Deliberate or not, it means one control has two appearances; worth a sentence in the CSS comment either way.
- **Sandboxed iframes.** Canvas and Moodle embed handouts in `<iframe sandbox>`; without `allow-downloads` the click does nothing and Chrome logs a console message that is not a `pageerror`, so no build or test notices. There is no clean feature detection. One line in AUTHORING.md is the whole fix.
- **Non-issue, flagged so nobody spends time on it:** cloned `<script>` elements carry the "already started" flag, so the clone's scripts would not run if reinserted into a live document. Irrelevant here — the clone is serialized, never inserted, and the flag is not a serialized attribute. The downloaded copy's scripts run normally.

---

## Verdict

**PASS WITH CONDITIONS.** The core design is right, and I say that with measurement behind it: replacing head and container from a parse-time capture is genuinely the only way to undo hljs, mermaid and the tab builder, the serialize-reparse round trip is a fixed point in this repo's own Chromium, downloading a downloaded copy does not compound, and the feature adds no path to withheld content — that last one holds by construction, because `hidden-filter.lua` deletes the AST nodes before HTML exists.

The conditions are three, and the first is the one I would not merge without. **Rewrite stn-bd3.3's byte assertions as DOM assertions before an implementer touches them** — as specified, all five are substring searches over a page that inlines the CSS and JS spelling every one of those names, so the criterion that guards the entire feature cannot pass and will be weakened into meaninglessness instead. **Name the button's glyph in the ticket and verify it against `undrawableCharacters`**, because a wrong choice breaks `make pdf` for every package of every consumer on upgrade, not just opted-in pages. And **stop capturing the head as a string** — it is 2.4 MB per page for a single cytoscape stylesheet append that a `childNodes.length` snapshot reverts for free, and the same snapshot trick applied to `<body>` turns the three-item chrome denylist into something that stays correct when a fourth widget arrives.</result>
```

````text
## 1. The head truncation assumes append-only. Cytoscape prepends. (Measured)

`~/Documents/Repositories/stencil/.claude/worktrees/stn-ejv-show-download/stencil/templates/_download.html.j2` states the premise explicitly:

> Every head mutation in play between now and a click is an append -- only cytoscape's stylesheet injection, and only for cytoscape-backed diagrams -- so truncating the clone's head back to this count reverts all of them for free.

The one mutation it names is a **prepend**. From the repo's own vendored `stencil/assets/mermaid.min.js` (11.17.2), at byte 1648337:

```js
var a = i.head, o = "__________cytoscape_stylesheet";
if (i.getElementById(o) == null) {
  var h = i.createElement("style"); h.id = o;
  h.textContent = ".__________cytoscape_container { position: relative; }";
  a.insertBefore(h, a.children[0]);
}
```

I ran that bundle in a real Chromium (Playwright, `mermaid.run()` over a page with a `mindmap` block — an `architecture-beta` is *not* required to reach it):

```
before: 7   after: 8   cytoStyle: true
headKids: ["#text(\"\\n\")", "STYLE#__________cytoscape_stylesheet", "META",
           "#text(\"\\n\")", "TITLE", "#text(\"\\n\")", "STYLE", "#text(\"\\n\")"]
```

The style lands at index 1, before `<meta charset>`. Bootstrap's bundle and highlight.js write to the head zero times (`document.head`, `getElementsByTagName("head")`, `head.insertBefore`, `head.appendChild` — all absent from both), so cytoscape is the whole population, and it is entirely on the wrong side of the assumption.

What this costs today. `while (cloneHead.childNodes.length > download.headCount) removeChild(lastChild)` removes one node from the **tail**. In both composition templates the head ends `...  </style>\n</head>`, so `head.lastChild` is a whitespace text node. The first prepend is therefore absorbed by that one node: the cytoscape `<style>` is *retained* in the download (the design promised to strip it, and "the downloaded bytes are the page pandoc wrote" becomes false for any page with a mindmap), and a newline is lost instead. Visible damage: none.

Why it still ranks first. The entire margin is one whitespace text node. A second head-prepending library, a second cytoscape-class injection in a future mermaid, or a consumer whose `_page-head.html.j2` or composition override ends `</style></head>` with no trailing newline, and the node removed from the tail is the page's own `<style>` — the whole inlined stylesheet. The downloaded file then opens, renders, and is unstyled, with no exception, no console message, and no failing test. That is the exact failure shape this repository's comments say it optimizes against.

Fix, smallest first:

- Make the truncation identity-checked rather than count-checked. Capture a signature of the last pristine head child (`document.head.lastChild.nodeName` plus, for an element, its `id`/first 64 chars of `textContent`), and after truncating verify the clone's new `lastChild` still matches it. If it does not, abort the truncation and leave the head intact — an extra injected `<style>` in the download is strictly better than a missing one.
- Better: at capture time set a marker attribute on each head **element** child, and on the clone remove every head element lacking the marker (then strip the marker). That reverts prepends and appends alike, and does not care what order anything arrives in.
- Either way, update the comment. "Every head mutation is an append" is the sentence that will keep this bug alive.

## 2. The filename cap truncates the extension it just appended (Measured)

`downloadFilename()` in the same file appends the suffix and *then* caps:

```js
if (lower.slice(-5) !== '.html' && lower.slice(-4) !== '.htm') cleaned = cleaned + '.html';
return cleaned.slice(0, 200);
```

I ran the function verbatim in node over a spread of pathnames:

| pathname | result | ends in .htm(l)? |
|---|---|---|
| 196 `a` + `.html` | 200 chars, ends `.htm` | yes, but silently renamed |
| 210 `a` + `.html` | 200 chars, **no extension at all** | no |
| 198 `a`, no extension | ends `.h` | no |

Deterministic, ASCII-only, no unusual input required beyond a long file name. The saved file has no extension, so it does not open in a browser on double-click and the reader has no idea why.

Fix: cap the **stem**, then append. `cleaned = cleaned.slice(0, 195) + '.html'` (or compute the budget from the suffix length) rather than capping the finished name.

The other half of the same line: the cap is 200 **characters** and the comment's own stated limit is ~255 **bytes**. Measured: 90 CJK characters is 275 UTF-8 bytes — past the threshold, into the silent-cancel path the cap exists to avoid (my own prior measurement in a headless Chrome: a 400-char name produces `state: "canceled"`, no file, no error). And `slice(0, 200)` can land mid-surrogate: `"x" + "😀"×120 + ".html"` sliced at 200 ends on a lone high surrogate `\ud83d`. Use `new TextEncoder().encode(s).length` to measure and trim at a code-point boundary. This half is rare in practice; the extension-stripping half is not, and both are the same three-line fix.

The rest of the sanitizer holds up under attack. Decoding before splitting is the right order; `/%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2fetc/passwd` yields `passwd.html`, `/...` yields `document.html`, `/....html` yields `html.html`, the RLO character is stripped, a malformed `%ZZ` is passed through undecoded rather than thrown, and `.htm`/`.HTML` are both recognised. No traversal, no injection.

## 3. The body whitelist is keyed to this repository's own body shape

```js
var keep = child.classList.contains('container') ||
           child.classList.contains('theme-toggle-host') ||
           child.tagName === 'SCRIPT';
```

`AGENTS.md` documents composition templates as a consumer interface, and `_download.html.j2`'s own header says a consumer "is free to spell [`.container`] differently". It handles one consequence of that (no `.container` found → no button, which is the right call) and not the other two:

- A consumer whose overridden `html-template.html.j2` puts anything else at body level — a `<header>`, a `<footer>`, a skip link, a print watermark — has it **silently deleted from every downloaded copy**. The page still opens; it is just missing a piece.
- Worse: a consumer whose wrapper is named something else (`.page`, say) *and* whose author writes a raw-HTML or fenced `<div class="container">` inside the content. `.container` is a Bootstrap layout class and Bootstrap is inlined into every page, so an author reaching for it is unremarkable. The capture then grabs the author's inner div; on click, the clone's `.container` resolves to that same inner div and is replaced correctly — but the surrounding `.page` wrapper fails the whitelist and is removed, taking the whole document with it. The result is a syntactically valid HTML file containing an empty theme host, the scripts, and one stray fragment. A button that appears, works, and produces a near-empty file is the worst outcome in the space.

Fix that removes the class coupling entirely: at parse time, mark each `document.body` child with an attribute (`data-stencil-pristine`), and on the clone keep a child if it carries the marker **or** is a `SCRIPT` (the scripts below the capture point are not in the DOM yet — which is exactly why the count trick was rejected here, and the marker sidesteps it). Strip the marker from the survivors before serializing, and mark after capturing `containerEl.outerHTML` so it does not land in the captured string. That is robust against a consumer's layout, against runtime prepends, and against whatever a future release appends — the property the comment says it wants.
````

````text
# Record agent provenance on the ticket

A ticket's notes are the only durable record of HOW a change was produced. Six
months on, "why does this test assert X" is often answerable only by reading the
instruction the implementer was actually given — and a paraphrase reconstructed
later is exactly the kind of unverified claim that gets things wrong. Briefs also
explain **absences**: one that said "leave the empty-recipe case alone" tells the
next reader a gap was a decision, not an oversight.

## Step 0 — Preflight

```bash
python3 "~/.claude/plugins/cache/foundry/foundry/1.4.0/bin/preflight" --skill agent-record-provenance
```

## Step 1 — Find the session

Subagent transcripts live under
`~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/<session-id>/subagents/`. Ask the tool, which
owns the slug rule:

```bash
python3 "~/.claude/plugins/cache/foundry/foundry/1.4.0/bin/agent-provenance" sessions
```

It prints the slug it derived, the directory it looked under, and each session
holding transcripts (newest first, with a transcript count).

Do not hand-roll this as `pwd | tr / -`. Claude Code replaces **every**
non-alphanumeric character with a hyphen, not just the separator — so any
checkout path containing a dot, underscore, or space resolves to a directory
that does not exist. That matters immediately rather than theoretically: agents
run in `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<id>`, and the naive rule finds no worktree
session at all.

The newest is usually the current session, but confirm rather than assume — a
long-running piece of work can span several.

## Step 2 — Collect

```bash
python3 "~/.claude/plugins/cache/foundry/foundry/1.4.0/bin/agent-provenance" collect --session <session-dir>
```

This streams each transcript line by line and prints aggregates plus dispatch
text. **Never read a transcript yourself** — they run to megabytes, and one in
the session that prompted this rule was 3.4 MB. **Never retype a brief by hand.**

Review the output for anything that must not become a ticket note: credentials,
personal data, internal-only URLs. The tool refuses to render on obvious
credential shapes, but that check is a backstop for the unmistakable cases, not a
substitute for reading.

To redact, rerun `render` with `--redact-secrets`: each detected credential
becomes a `[REDACTED: <kind>]` marker while everything around it stays verbatim,
and the tool reports the agent id and dispatch index of every replacement on
stderr, so the substitution is auditable. Redacting in the renderer rather than
by hand means the secret never has to be handled again — passing it back on a
command line would leak it into shell history and `ps` — and the unredacted copy
stays only where the transcripts live.

For anything the pattern list cannot catch (personal data, an internal-only
URL), there is no automatic path: edit the rendered file before appending it.
**Never put a secret in a ticket field to satisfy this skill** — a redacted
brief still answers the question the record exists for; a leaked key cannot be
un-leaked.

`set -euo pipefail` and `mktemp` are load-bearing, not ceremony: without them a
failed render leaves an empty file that the append step still writes,
producing a blank provenance note that reads as "no agents ran" — and a fixed
`/tmp` path makes two concurrent runs share one file.

By default this selects agents whose dispatches name the ticket. Pass
`--ticket-pattern` for a non-beads id scheme (`'[A-Z]+-\d+'` for Jira), or
`--all-agents` when every agent in the session served this one ticket.

Render and append in ONE block, because a separate Bash tool call is a
separate shell: the `trap` below deletes `$out` the moment this shell exits,
so an append step in a later block would read a file that no longer exists.
Append atomically, and only once. Never read-modify-write:

```bash

out=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$out"' EXIT

  --session <session-dir> --ticket <ticket-id> > "$out"
````
